evidence.scope: cli.state_for resolves a ticket by its id rather than by the filename recorded when the journal started, and reports which of the three sources it used; the edge is that nothing else changes, not the records, not the questions, not the thresholds, and no journal already written becomes invalid.
acceptance: state_for reads the ticket at the recorded path when it exists and records the source: a unit test builds a journal whose recorded path exists, asserts the ticket text is the file's and the source reads as the recorded path.

When the recorded path is gone, state_for finds the ticket at docs/tickets/<ID>-*.md and records that it did: a unit test renames the ticket file under a temporary root and asserts the text is the renamed file's, not the snapshot's.
The snapshot is used only when no file matches, and the state says so: a unit test removes the ticket entirely and asserts the text is the snapshot and the source names it as a snapshot.
Two files matching the id is a refusal naming the candidates: a unit test writes two SEEN-XXX-*.md files and asserts the HarnessError lists both paths.

SEEN-096's clarify record re-asked against the ticket that now exists, with the score recorded here: a note in this journal carrying the number, run through the live API, which is why it is a note and not a test.

The skill's fourth rule tells a session to name an unknowable in decisions: the file says so, sync has regenerated both copies, and the rule is verified by this very record, which was refused for following the old advice.
decisions: Resolve by id rather than recording renames as journal records, because the id is already in every record and the filename is derived from it; more machinery would buy nothing. Taken by the implementer, 24 September 2026.

Report the source in the state rather than only in the code, because a judgement made against a snapshot and one made against the live ticket are different evidence and a reader of the journal cannot otherwise tell them apart. Taken by the implementer.

An ambiguous id refuses rather than picking the newest or the first match. The harness refuses when it cannot know, which is the rule SEEN-086 set and every stage has followed since. Taken by the implementer.

Keep the snapshot fallback rather than refusing outright when a ticket is deleted, because a delivered ticket's journal must stay readable after its file is archived, and history and report both read old journals. Taken by the implementer.

The fix is carried by its own ticket rather than by SEEN-096, on the founder's standing pattern: the gate that is misjudging a ticket cannot be repaired by that ticket. SEEN-096 tried and was refused at 0.46, recorded in its journal at record 11. Authority: Ruud, twice, on SEEN-100 and on the SEEN-089 split.

Whether SEEN-096's clarify record clears 0.8 once the gate reads the ticket that exists cannot be known before the fix is in; proceed anyway, because the fix is right whether it then clears or not, and re-ask it before review with the number recorded here either way. If it still does not clear, that is SEEN-096's evidence to act on, not a reason to hold this ticket.

Whether any other journal carries a stale ticket path is not known yet; proceed, and settle it by reading record 1 of every journal and testing each recorded path, with the answer recorded here before review. It cannot change the fix, only the size of what the fix repairs.

SEEN-100's fourth rule in the skill is corrected here rather than in a ticket of its own. It told a session to leave a named unknown in open_questions, and the code layer of this same gate refuses a non-empty open_questions. This record was refused for following it, one hour after it shipped. Taken by the implementer, 24 September 2026.
